guidelines.detail: refines ACT-05 (The description and missing-flow records support waiting for order completion alongside other work, then synchronizing before continuing. ACT-05 distinguishes message tasks from message events; this guideline refines it by specifying how to model an awaited completion during concurrent work.)

same as LRN-028 (The description says the process begins with a desire to build, while the generated start-event label implies the activity is already underway. This supports a general guideline for intention-based triggers. It is already covered essentially by learned guideline LRN-028.)

refines COL-01 (The description establishes the architect’s response and the stores’ order processing as actions by outside participants, supporting separate pools and interactions. The generated architect pool and outgoing flow show a modeling choice difference, not simply an absent participant. COL-01 already covers distinct interacting participants; this guideline refines when to recognize an outside party as )

same as LRN-063 (The description says the process begins with wanting to build, while the generated start-event label says the building activity has begun. LRN-063 already covers representing an initiating goal or intention with a start event; this wording makes the label implication explicit. The other label pairs do not establish a separate general guideline.)

same as LRN-074 (The description explicitly says a request is sent to the architect and a draft is returned. The generated pool “Tree house architect” appears to represent the reference “Architect” pool, so the evidenced gap is the missing message flows, not a missing participant pool. This guideline is already covered by LRN-074.)

refines FID-01 (The description explicitly states that the prepared materials are ordered. The reference includes a distinct ordering task, while the generated model has no counterpart and omits the flow after preparation. This specifies how to apply FID-01 to ordering or submission actions.)

same as LRN-070 (The label pairs show differences in actions or stated scope, including sending messages versus calling and processing an order versus getting one. The description provides the basis for preserving those meanings. LRN-070 already expresses essentially the same guideline.)

same as LRN-074 (The description states that an outside participant receives requirements and returns a draft. The records show the expected participant and message flows lack counterparts, while a differently named generated pool exists; the exchange is therefore not fully represented. This guideline is already covered essentially by learned guideline LRN-074.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an external response or completion is awaited while other work can proceed in parallel: Model the awaited response or completion as an intermediate catch event on a parallel branch, and synchronize that branch with the other work before continuing.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an external response or completion is awaited while other work can proceed in parallel

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states what initiates the process or identifies the outcome at which it ends: Label the corresponding start or end event with a concise phrase that faithfully names that stated boundary, rather than a generic label or a related intermediate activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents a desire, goal, or intention as the process trigger

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an outside participant performs work of its own or returns information after receiving input, rather than merely naming that participant as a recipient or source: Model that participant as a separate pool and represent the described exchanges with message flows between valid interaction nodes; keep the initiating participant’s work in its own pool.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an outside participant performs work of its own or returns information after receiving input, rather than merely naming that participant as a recipient or source

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description identifies a concrete action that initiates the process: Model that action as an activity after the start event, and connect it by sequence flow to the next described activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a concrete action uses information or materials produced by an earlier activity.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an initiating goal or intent, followed by preparatory work that must happen before the primary operation begins: Represent the initiating goal or intent with a start event, and model each stated preparatory action as an activity before the primary operation.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a desire or intention to perform an activity as the process trigger, without saying that the activity has begun

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that prepared items are subsequently ordered or submitted in a transaction: Model placing or submitting the order as a distinct activity sequenced after the preparation activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that prepared items are subsequently ordered or submitted in a transaction

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity, its object, scope, or recipient: Label the corresponding BPMN element so that it preserves the described action, object, scope, and direction; do not replace them with a related action or add unsupported details.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity or event with a recognizable action, object, or scope
